evidence.text: At the lower-left entry, the printed headword is 茶, followed by the parenthetical form 茶 and the reading tú. Its entry text begins “形声字。从艸，齊声。本义是指蓼科植物名。” The entry continues at the top-right of the same page after the lower-left column ends, beginning “引申之亦可比喻苦、痛。” The top running header contains 茶 among other headwords; it is not body text. Page 72 starts unrelated entries and does not continue this 茶 account. Direct scan inspection resolves the body headword as 茶, not 荼.

evidence.field: 余 headword and independent account; direct visual inspection
evidence.text: The page has a distinct 余 headword with reading yú. Its text calls the graph pictographic, says the oracle-bone form resembles a dwelling supported by a wooden post, and gives an original dwelling sense; it also notes use as a first-person pronoun. This confirms the reported standalone 余 entry. That account does not itself establish sound function in 茶 or 荼.

evidence.source: 臺灣教育部《異體字字典》, Tea headword A03475
evidence.text: The dictionary identifies standard 茶 as 艹-06-10 and specifies upper 艹 with four strokes and lower 木: the vertical stroke of 木 is unhooked, with left and right strokes disconnected from it. It also quotes an older view that 茶 is a reduced form of 荼, while noting that 茶 and 荼 now have distinct standard forms and different readings/meanings. Thus the literal lower component of current standard 茶 is 木, not 余. Historical phonetic 余 and present lower 木 must not be conflated. The cited page does not itself establish the detailed graphic reduction path.
evidence.title: A03475 茶 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 臺灣教育部《異體字字典》, 荼 headword A03494
evidence.field: transmitted Shuowen form and phonetic role
evidence.text: The entry quotes 大徐本: “苦葵也。从艸，余聲” and 段注本: “苦荼也。从艸，余聲.” This is an explicit sound-role statement for 余 in 荼. It is not an assertion about 余’s role in current 茶, and any comparison must use the pronunciation of 荼 rather than transferring the 茶 reading to the 荼 record.
evidence.title: A03494 荼 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The database says 茶 is a later graph, earlier written 荼, analyzed as 艸 plus phonetic 余; it gives the original meaning as tea tree and cites Tang-period usages. This supports the historical analysis but does not justify describing current lower strokes as literally 余.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：茶

No source-bound record ID for the provisional corpus page 71 was provided in the packet, so the OCR producer must resolve it against its page-id/source hashes. Scan PDF p. 72 directly shows the distinct 荼 headword and a separate 荼 formation statement. The scanned page 71 formation text itself gives 齊 as phonetic; do not silently normalize this printed form or infer 余 from the later discussion.

The article’s current 茶 component form requires correction: current standard lower component is 木 per the official Taiwan Ministry of Education character-form entry. The draft’s historical 余 phonetic analysis may be retained as attributed historical analysis, but should not be represented as the literal lower part of present-day standard 茶. Whether lower 木 is a reduced/replaced descendant of a historical 余 component is a separate historical relationship and should remain qualified; sources inspected here do not fully establish that precise transformation.

Historical 荼 sound record referent mismatch: the supplied component sound comparison pairs 余 with 茶 reading *rlaː, while the claim is scoped to 荼. The official dictionary explicitly assigns 余 as phonetic in 荼 but does not give a same-system Old Chinese reconstruction pair for 荼 and 余. No readily inspected primary same-system pair was established in this pass; do not substitute 茶’s value for 荼 or carry that sound array to the 荼-host record.

The local-primary reading table supplies modern Mandarin 余 yú, 茶 chá, 荼 tú and the official dictionary pages display these current readings, but no primary same-system ancient reconstruction pair for 荼/余 was obtained here.
